EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The most critical development in the past 24 hours is the significant escalation of tensions in the Strait of Hormuz and increased military readiness across the region. This includes multiple reported drone incidents between US and Iranian forces, a US defense report detailing billions in war costs and equipment losses, and a secret meeting of US, Israeli, and Arab military commanders to discuss the conflict with Iran. Concurrently, Saudi Arabia has canceled oil shipments to Europe following Houthi attacks and sought intelligence assistance from Israel.

IRAN
The war with Iran has reportedly cost the United States between $33.4 billion and $40 billion, according to various reports. A Pentagon assessment indicated that Iranian strikes damaged or destroyed hundreds of US military facilities and infrastructure across the region, leading to strategic shortages in US munitions and the destruction or damage of multiple advanced aircraft, including 4 F-15Es, 1 F-35A, 1 A-10, 12 KC-135s, and over 30 MQ-9 drones. Iran has expanded earth fortifications at the "Enchanted Mountain" (Har ha-Makhshaf) in August, reportedly in response to US President Trump's threats of attack. Mohsen Rezaei, Secretary of Iran's Supreme National Security Council, stated that the "rules of the game" around oil and strategic straits have changed, asserting no talks will occur until Iran's demands are fully met.

In the Strait of Hormuz, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) claimed to have shot down three US MQ-1 Predator drones today, with one source claiming a fourth was also destroyed. Simultaneously, US officials stated that a US drone destroyed two Iranian small boats in the Strait of Hormuz yesterday after IRGC forces attempted to seize an American naval drone, resulting in the deaths of most crew members. Separately, a Panamanian-flagged oil tanker, the "El Gaia," reportedly exploded after hitting a naval mine in the Strait of Hormuz, with two crew members missing, although the US Central Command (CENTCOM) claims the vessel was previously hit by an Iranian missile last month and then a drone last weekend.

Behrouz Kamalvandi, spokesperson for the Atomic Energy Organization of Iran (AEOI), reiterated Iran's commitment to its peaceful nuclear program at the IAEA conference, stating that Iran would not surrender and that nuclear science cannot be destroyed by aggression. He also stated that Iran has a natural right to conceal sensitive nuclear sites during ongoing aggression. Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi claimed that "hundreds of US military sites" have been "blown to pieces" and "dozens of aircraft scorched," and is scheduled to visit China tomorrow, September 16. Iran was elected to the general committee of the 70th IAEA general conference in a secret ballot, despite US opposition. Iran has outlined 2026 civil defense plans for three scenarios: the end of war, a ceasefire, and full-scale war. The head of Iran's Atomic Energy Organization, Mohammad Eslami, was denied entry to Vienna for the IAEA conference due to a UN travel ban. The Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK) met with Iran's Foreign Minister and reiterated that Iraqi Kurdistan's territory will not be used to threaten Iran. Tribal leaders and scholars have condemned the assassination of Molavi Yousef Gorgij, a Sunni cleric in Sistan and Baluchestan Province, with his funeral scheduled for tomorrow in Zahedan. An Iranian Boeing 737 made an emergency return to Mashhad after a reported tire burst and engine damage. The IRGC Navy announced that the Strait of Hormuz is closed and under its intelligence control, warning any vessels entering "unsafe routes" would face incidents. The US Department of Justice alleges that Iran laundered millions of dollars in oil revenue through the cryptocurrency exchange Binance.

ISRAEL
The Trump administration is preparing for a potential $2.8 billion deal to sell 40,000 2,000-pound bombs to Israel, which would be the largest such sale in years. Israeli military operations in Gaza resulted in the killing of Mohsen Farid Said Abu Hadaf, a Palestinian Islamic Jihad rocket squad commander involved in the October 7, 2023, onslaught in the Kissufim area. The IDF also killed Ahmad al-Batash, commander of Hamas's Jabalia Battalion in northern Gaza, and two other Hamas commanders, Rafat Abu Zamar (company commander in operations division) and Muhammad Khader Fahmi Aghour (weapons production), both of whom allegedly violated the ceasefire and advanced attacks.

Moshe Edri, head of Israel's Atomic Energy Committee, speaking at the IAEA General Conference, warned that Iran's "extreme regime" continues to build missile infrastructure and advance a military nuclear program, stating that Israel "will not stand idly by" against threats to its existence. Israeli Ambassador to the UN, Gilad Erdan, called for a boycott of the Durban conference, calling it a platform for antisemitism and anti-Israel campaigns. The Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu condemned the documentary "NZA," exposing IDF conduct in Gaza, as "intolerable" and "global anti-Semitic incitement," with ministers reportedly seeking to revoke the directors' citizenship. The IDF Chief of Staff has launched an investigation into anonymous testimonies featured in the film.

Domestic political tensions continue, with Avigdor Lieberman, head of Yisrael Beiteinu, criticizing Ofer Winter for his inability to "decide in three years." Winter accused the Likud party of sending private investigators to monitor his party members, a claim the Likud called "absolutely false" and threatened with a libel suit. An activist, Alon Li Green, was arrested following protests regarding an illegal outpost in the Galilee, which the Jewish National Fund (KKL) ordered dismantled. Residents of Karmiel were advised to boil drinking water due to abnormal sampling results. A 19-year-old Israeli Arab from Kafr Qasim was arrested by Shin Bet for planning a terror attack, influenced by October 7 events, targeting an Amdocs server farm. A suspected ramming attack occurred near Ariel with no casualties reported.

GAZA & WEST BANK
Israeli military operations in Gaza focused on eliminating key commanders. Mohsen Farid Said Abu Hadaf, a Palestinian Islamic Jihad rocket squad commander involved in the October 7, 2023, attacks, was killed in Khan Younis. Ahmad al-Batash, the commander of Hamas's Jabalia Battalion, was killed in an airstrike in northern Gaza. Rafat Abu Zamar, a company commander in Hamas's operations division, and Muhammad Khader Fahmi Aghour, involved in weapons production for Hamas, were also killed in separate strikes in Khan Younis and Gaza City, respectively. The IDF stated these individuals advanced terror activities and restored Hamas capabilities "in systematic violation of the ceasefire."

A senior UK minister stated that they "will no longer stand by while innocent Palestinians are killed in Gaza and the West Bank." Press TV reporter Naqqa Hamed was abducted by Israeli forces at a military checkpoint near Bethlehem in the occupied West Bank. Victims of the October 7, 2023, attacks presented a detailed "Case 7.10" report, accusing previous Israeli governments of responsibility for the failures leading to the events.

LEBANON
Israeli forces operating in the Lebanese side of Mount Dov located a Hezbollah rocket launcher with 32 rockets and several projectiles, as well as a fighting position and tunnel shaft. These armaments were likely left behind before the April ceasefire. Lebanese sources reported Israeli artillery strikes in the areas of Froun and Ali al-Taher in southern Lebanon.

Lebanese Prime Minister Nawaf Salam reported that the cost of recent conflicts has exceeded $20 billion and is expected to surpass $27 billion, excluding indirect damages. He detailed approximately 9,000 fatalities, over 30,000 injuries, and over one million displaced individuals, with tens of thousands of destroyed buildings and 75 villages still uninhabitable. Lebanon has requested to postpone planned talks with Israel in Rome due to the security escalation near Ali al-Taher. The Lebanese Ministry of Education alleged that the Israeli army destroyed the Mohammad Fakih state school in the village of Tebnine on the day school was meant to start. Lebanese prosecutors have reportedly requested that former President Michel Aoun be charged in connection with the 2020 Beirut port explosion. Heitham Tabtabai, a senior member of Hezbollah's military wing, who previously fought with the Houthis in Yemen, was reportedly killed by the IDF.

SYRIA & IRAQ
The US Department of State notified Congress of a re-allocation of $52 million in aid from Middle Eastern and Eastern European countries, including Iraq, Tunisia, Slovakia, and North Macedonia, to Latin American nations. Iraq's Prime Minister stated that investigations into the targeting of Saudi Arabia are underway, and Iraq reaffirmed it would not allow its territory to be used to attack other regional countries. Bafel Talabani, leader of the Patriotic Union of Kurdistan (PUK), met with Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi in Tehran, discussing economic ties, border security, and counter-terrorism efforts, with a commitment that Iraqi Kurdistan would not be used against Iran.

Protests have erupted in several Syrian cities following a sharp increase in fuel prices. British air forces were observed active in the skies over Mosul, Iraq. Reports indicated unknown drone attacks on Rawanduz in Erbil province, Iraqi Kurdistan, and a drone crash inside a camp of the Kurdish Democratic Party of Iran (KDPI) in Balisan. The German Chancellor encouraged Baghdad to "firmly" disarm militias. The Iraqi Ministry of Education postponed the start of the academic year until October 11.

GULF STATES
Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman met with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi in Cairo. They agreed to implement mechanisms to ensure freedom of navigation in the strategic Straits of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandeb. Houthi military spokesperson Yahya Saree claimed that the Saudi Air Force conducted 52 airstrikes in the last 24 hours, using F-15 and Typhoon jets from Khamis Mushait and Taif bases, targeting civilian infrastructure in Taiz, Al-Jawf, Al-Bayda, Saada, and Amran provinces, vowing retaliation. The Saudi-led coalition, in turn, reported that Houthi ballistic missiles and drones struck civilian sites in Khamis Mushait, Abha, and Taif on September 14, injuring 13 civilians and damaging homes and vehicles, promising a "firm response."

Early warning alerts for potential missile attacks were activated across multiple Saudi cities, including Mecca, Jeddah, Taif, Yanbu, Abha, Khamis Mushait, Al Ula, and Jazan. These alarms reportedly lasted for about half an hour before "all clear" messages were issued. Saudi Arabia conducted an airstrike on a Houthi communications tower in Yemen and intensified air operations across Al-Jawf, Marib, Al-Hudayda, Saada, and Taiz.

Saudi Arabia informed some European oil refiners that their September-loading crude cargoes have been canceled following the closure of the East-West pipeline, which was attacked by Houthis. Oil loadings have been suspended at Yanbu, Saudi Arabia's main Red Sea port, following the pipeline incident, with suspicions of a direct Houthi attack on the Yanbu refinery. The US Energy Secretary anticipates the East-West pipeline to be operational "very soon."

Saudi Arabia has requested intelligence assistance from Israel, facilitated by US CENTCOM, to counter Houthi attacks. The UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham is considering military aid to Saudi Arabia, including deploying military advisors, with reports of 100 senior military advisors being sent immediately. US officials confirmed Washington has so far resisted Saudi requests for direct military intervention beyond intelligence support. The Foreign Minister of Oman discussed regional developments with his US counterpart. The CEO of Oman LNG expressed optimism that the crisis in the Strait of Hormuz would end soon.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **US-Israel-Arab Military Summit**: Top military commanders from the US, Israel, Saudi Arabia, UAE, Bahrain, Kuwait, Qatar, Jordan, and Egypt held a secret meeting in Germany last week to discuss the war with Iran and regional security, hosted by CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper. This marks the first such meeting since the US and Israel began operations against Iran.
2.  **Major US Bomb Sale to Israel**: The Trump administration is preparing a $2.8 billion deal to sell 40,000 2,000-pound bombs to Israel, which would be the largest single sale of such munitions in recent years.
3.  **US War Costs and Damages Report**: A Pentagon inspector general's report revealed that the war with Iran has cost the US approximately $33.4 billion, caused strategic shortages in munitions, and resulted in the damage or destruction of hundreds of US military facilities and multiple advanced aircraft, including 4 F-15Es, 1 F-35A, 1 A-10, 12 KC-135s, and over 30 MQ-9 drones.
4.  **Strait of Hormuz Incidents**: Iran claimed shooting down three to four US MQ-1 Predator drones over the Strait of Hormuz today. Concurrently, US officials claimed destroying two Iranian small boats yesterday after an IRGC attempt to seize an American naval drone, killing most on board.
5.  **Saudi Oil Supply Disruptions**: Saudi Arabia notified some European oil refiners of canceled September crude oil cargoes following the closure of its East-West pipeline and intensified Houthi attacks. Oil loadings have been suspended at Yanbu, a major Red Sea port.
6.  **Saudi-Israel Intelligence Cooperation**: Saudi Arabia formally requested intelligence assistance from Israel, mediated by US CENTCOM, to help counter ongoing Houthi drone and missile attacks.
7.  **Escalating Houthi Attacks on Saudi Arabia**: Houthi forces launched widespread missile and drone attacks on Saudi cities, triggering early warning alerts in Mecca, Jeddah, Taif, Yanbu, Abha, Khamis Mushait, Al Ula, and Jazan.
8.  **Targeted Killings in Gaza**: The IDF killed several senior Hamas and Palestinian Islamic Jihad (PIJ) commanders in Gaza, including Mohsen Farid Said Abu Hadaf (PIJ rocket squad commander), Ahmad al-Batash (Hamas Jabalia Battalion commander), Rafat Abu Zamar (Hamas company commander), and Muhammad Khader Fahmi Aghour (Hamas weapons producer).

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks are high across multiple flashpoints. The secret meeting between US, Israeli, and Arab military commanders to discuss the war with Iran indicates a potential for broader coordinated action. The impending $2.8 billion US bomb sale to Israel, alongside Iran's reported expansion of fortifications at the "Enchanted Mountain," suggests both sides are preparing for intensified conflict. The Strait of Hormuz remains a critical flashpoint, with claims of Iranian drone shoot-downs and US destruction of Iranian boats, coupled with the "El Gaia" tanker incident and Iran's declaration of the strait being under its intelligence control.

The ongoing Houthi missile and drone attacks on Saudi Arabia, including cities like Mecca and Yanbu, and Saudi retaliation, signify an active and dangerous conflict. The UK's consideration and immediate deployment of military advisors to Saudi Arabia, following warnings of "catastrophic" consequences if the Bab al-Mandeb strait is controlled by Houthis, highlights regional instability. Israel's Atomic Energy Committee head, Moshe Edri, explicitly stated that Israel "will not stand idly by" against threats to its existence or Iran's military nuclear program, outlining a potential red line. Mohsen Rezaei's insistence that no talks with the US will occur until all Iranian demands are met signals a rigid stance from Tehran. The Pentagon report detailing extensive US military losses and munitions depletion underscores the high cost and strain of the current conflict, potentially influencing future military posture.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
**United States**: The US war with Iran has cost between $33.4 billion and $40 billion, leading to strategic shortages in advanced munitions and significant damage to US military assets. The Trump administration is preparing to sell $2.8 billion worth of 2,000-pound bombs to Israel. It has also re-directed $52 million in military aid from countries like Iraq and Tunisia to Latin American nations. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated that the US is "ending" the threat from Iran, not just managing it, and has engaged in "constructive private talks" with China and the UAE regarding cutting off Iranian finances. President Trump attributed rising fuel prices to the conflict and urged allies to reimburse the US for protecting shipping in the Strait of Hormuz. The US confirmed it has deployed space control weapons. The FBI arrested a 21-year-old in Pennsylvania suspected of planning an ISIS-inspired attack.
**Gulf States**: Saudi Arabia is grappling with intensified Houthi attacks, leading to widespread early warning alerts across its cities and the cancellation of some September crude oil shipments to Europe. Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman met with Egyptian President Abdel Fattah al-Sisi, agreeing on mechanisms to ensure freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandeb. Saudi Arabia has requested intelligence assistance from Israel, mediated by CENTCOM, to counter Houthi threats. The UAE's Foreign Minister discussed regional stability with his Egyptian counterpart. Oman's Foreign Minister spoke with the US Secretary of State regarding regional developments.
**European Union Members**: Denmark summoned the Russian ambassador after a Russian frigate fired flares at a Danish military helicopter. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen affirmed the EU's resolve against Russia is strengthening. France is reportedly pressuring the EU to remove Russian-Uzbek oligarch Alisher Usmanov from the sanctions list, a move potentially linked to the release of French prisoners in Azerbaijan. Germany's Chancellor Friedrich Merz canceled a US trip due to increasing political tensions at home. A drone crashed near a German airbase in Wunstorf, its origin unknown.
**Russia**: Putin's special advisor, Nikolai Patrushev, warned that Poland would "cease to exist" within "two or three days" if it engaged in war with Russia. Russia's Defence Ministry claimed to strike a tanker in the Ukrainian port of Izmail.
**China**: Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi is scheduled to visit China tomorrow. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent reported "good private talks" with China regarding Iran's financial activities, with further discussions expected between Trump and Xi Jinping at an upcoming summit. China's intelligence chief, Chen Yixin, published an article warning that the advancement of AI could directly threaten the Chinese Communist Party's rule. China urged the US to cease preparing for war in outer space following Washington's confirmation of weapon deployment in orbit.
**Turkey**: Turkey's Foreign Minister expressed growing concern about the Ukraine war extending to the Black Sea region. The Turkish parliament is expected to ratify the Mecca agreement in about a month.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
There are contradictions regarding the cost of the US war with Iran, with figures ranging from $33.4 billion (Pentagon report) to $40 billion (N12) and $38 billion (NAYA). The specific figure of $33.4 billion from the Pentagon report is presented as the most authoritative source from the raw data.
The incident in the Strait of Hormuz involving the tanker "El Gaia" has conflicting narratives: the IRGC claims it hit a naval mine, while US CENTCOM asserts it was previously struck by an Iranian missile and then a drone. Oman confirmed the incident and reported two missing crew members.
Iran's claims of shooting down three to four US MQ-1 drones over the Strait of Hormuz and the US claim of destroying two Iranian boats after an attempted seizure of a US naval drone could refer to separate events or differing interpretations of the same. The US also claimed "most" on board the Iranian boats were killed, while Iranian media reported attacks on "fishing boats" with "missing" fishermen.
Several claims lack independent verification, including the Houthi spokesperson's figures for Saudi airstrikes (52 in 24 hours) and his vow for retaliation, as well as the Houthi claim to "liberate Mecca." Conversely, Saudi reports detailing 13 civilian injuries from Houthi attacks are also from an involved party.
The assertion by "kianmeli1" that "military centers evacuated at 11:00" today and "today we almost went to war" is unverified and not corroborated by other sources. Similarly, the claim that Trump refused to take MBS's phone call for 48 hours is from a single source and unverified.
The Iraqi Prime Minister stated that investigations into the targeting of Saudi Arabia are ongoing, without attributing responsibility for any attacks.
There are reporting gaps regarding the precise nature and extent of damage to the "hundreds of US facilities" mentioned in the Pentagon report.
